data.text: The outcome of contextual inquiry can be used as design guidelines or functional requirements. Functional requirements are specified in terms of functions with well-defined inputs and outputs. This specification makes them easy to convert to code, making the transition to code design easier.
points: Contextual inquiry outcomes can be used as design guidelines or functional requirements.
Functional requirements have well-defined inputs and outputs, making them easy to convert to code.

data.text: Guidelines framed from observations are generic and specify what an application should or should not do rather than how to do it. Using guidelines based on observed behaviors includes those behaviors in the overall system to ensure the user is involved in the design based on observations and feedback.
points: Guidelines are generic and specify what an application should or should not do rather than how to do it.
Basing guidelines on observed behaviors ensures that users are involved in the design.

data.text: Functional requirements specify system features as black-box functions with well-defined inputs and outputs. Usability requirements can be converted into functional requirements to be directly incorporated into the code. These requirements are generally organized in a hierarchy within a software requirements specification (SRS). Additionally, notes from contextual inquiry can be used as design guidelines or converted into functional requirements.
points: Functional requirements specify system features as black-box functions with well-defined inputs and outputs.
Usability requirements can be converted into functional requirements to be directly incorporated into the code.
Requirements are generally organized in a hierarchy within a software requirements specification (SRS).
Contextual inquiry notes can be used as design guidelines or converted into functional requirements.

data.text: Usability requirements for the Majuli VR Tour were gathered through field trips, interviews, and observations. The system targets three non-resident user groups: students, tourists, and pilgrims, using contextual inquiry to identify their specific needs and design challenges. To prevent cybersickness and confusion, information is restricted to subsets tailored to each group's activities. Contextual inquiry also highlighted the importance of location awareness and interaction aids to provide a seamless experience.
points: Usability requirements were gathered through field trips, interviews, observations, and notes.
The tour targets three non-resident user groups: students, tourists, and pilgrims.
Contextual inquiry was used to identify group-specific needs, features, and design challenges.
Data is restricted to subsets per group to reduce confusion and cybersickness.
Contextual inquiry also identified the need for location awareness and interaction aids.

data.text: Contextual inquiry is one of many methods available for usability requirement gathering.
points: Contextual inquiry is one of many methods for gathering usability requirements.
